size_band: ~100 employees at peak, CLP 9,000M annual sales at peak
stage_or_date: March 2024 (forced liquidation and auction of the business)
the_problem: After the Municipality of Santiago forced owner Pablo Villalba to regularise his property lease in 2014 and shut the premises in 2015-16 (in December, 'el mejor del año'), the business was hit by the 2019 social unrest (looting, damage) and then COVID-19. Debts built up until creditors forced the company into liquidation.
the_decision: Pablo Villalba, who took over the 64-year-old distributor in 2002, kept the business running through nine years of decline, including a delivery-only model, instead of exiting. He told Las Últimas Noticias: "quise seguir, pagar mis deudas, no pude sacarme esta mala racha"; on the delivery pivot: "Mis ingresos eran de dos millones y medio mensuales con el delivery y pagaba de arriendo dos millones. Era insostenible".
the_outcome: Company forced into liquidation by creditors and its assets put up for auction; peak ~100 staff and >CLP 9,000M yearly sales fell to CLP 2.5M monthly delivery income against CLP 2M rent; 64 years of operation ended.
